items.title: Nvidia declines roughly 7.5% while AMD rallies 5.6% in AI-chip divergence
items.summary: Nvidia fell approximately 7.5% to $172.75 at 9:34 AM EST after its board opened an inquiry into allegations involving its CEO. AMD rose about 5.6% to $473.73 in early trading following an Oppenheimer upgrade. The sector split is a material repricing signal, though no change in Nvidia's underlying chip demand or output has been established.

items.title: Brent loss widens to about 3.9% while Hormuz security warnings remain active
items.summary: Brent dropped to approximately $94.48 per barrel, down 3.91% at 10:15 AM EST, extending the earlier 1.7% slide as traders reacted to conditional U.S.–Iran de-escalation remarks. Reuters earlier recorded WTI at $88.17, down 2.9%, at 7:19 AM EST. Maritime security risk remains elevated; no fresh physical oil-flow loss or verified normal transit restoration was established.

items.title: Google introduces TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max AI infrastructure systems
items.summary: Google announced two specialized configurations in its eighth-generation TPU portfolio: 8tx for confidential inference and 8i Max for large-context and memory-intensive agent workloads. These are system designs using existing TPU silicon, not wholly new chip architectures. Google cites nearly 100 TPU customers, but availability dates, incremental orders and market share gains were not established.

items.title: Constellation reports Q3 results and new nuclear power agreements
items.summary: Constellation reported Q3 adjusted operating EPS of $5.06 and narrowed 2026 guidance to $12.50–$12.80. It disclosed a Google nuclear collaboration, a 20-year 270 MW agreement and a conditional DOE commitment up to $5 billion. These strengthen long-duration power demand visibility, while financing and execution remain conditional.

items.title: Immunovant meets 600 mg rheumatoid arthritis trial primary endpoint
items.summary: IMVT-1402 at 600 mg met its Week 28 primary endpoint with 92.5% ACR20 response versus 75.6% placebo (p=0.0139) after an open-label lead-in. The 300 mg arm did not significantly outperform placebo. The result supports development, but the enriched withdrawal design and pending FDA discussions limit certainty.
